_meta.indication: MYQORZO is a cardiac myosin inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adults with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) to improve functional capacity and symptoms.

pivotal_trials.design: Placebo-controlled, double-blind, 1:1 randomized trial in adults with oHCM; treatment up to 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in pVO2 (peak oxygen consumption) by CPET from baseline to Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: pVO2 LS mean difference vs placebo 1.7 mL/kg/min (95% CI 1.0, 2.4), p<0.0001. KCCQ-CSS LS mean difference 7.3 points (95% CI 4.6, 10.1; p<0.0001). NYHA >=1 class improvement odds ratio 4.6 (95% CI 2.6, 8.5; p<0.0001) at Week 12. Valsalva LVOT-G treatment difference -48.4 mm Hg (95% CI -55.1, -41.7; p<0.0001) at Week 12.

key_safety: The most common adverse reaction was hypertension (8% vs 2% placebo), the only adverse reaction occurring in >5% of patients and more commonly on MYQORZO than placebo. The principal serious risk is heart failure due to systolic dysfunction (reduced LVEF).
target_moa: Aficamten is a small molecule, allosteric and reversible inhibitor of cardiac myosin; it reduces the force generated by myosin at the cardiac sarcomere, reducing cardiac sarcomere contractility and LVOT obstruction in oHCM patients.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF HEART FAILURE — MYQORZO can cause heart failure due to systolic dysfunction; echocardiogram assessments of LVEF are required before and during use; initiation in patients with LVEF <55% is not recommended.

rems.type: Because of the risk of heart failure due to systolic dysfunction, MYQORZO is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the MYQORZO REMS Program, with elements to assure safe use (ETASU).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; FDA determined a meeting was not needed as the application did not raise issues requiring external expert input.

summary.text: Aficamten was granted Orphan Drug Designation on January 5, 2021 and breakthrough therapy designation on December 6, 2021; the NDA was submitted as a rolling review (final portion received September 26, 2024) and approved with a REMS due to the risk of heart failure due to systolic dysfunction.

requirement.text: PMR 4900-1: A worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Myqorzo during pregnancy to assess risks of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant.

citations.quote: 4900-1 A worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Mycorzo during pregnancy to assess risks of pregnancy and maternal complications, and adverse effects on the developing fetus, the neonate, and the infant. Assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.

requirement.text: PMR 4900-2: A milk-only lactation study in lactating women who have received Myqorzo to measure concentrations of aficamten in breast milk using a validated assay.

citations.quote: 4900-2 A milk-only lactation study in lactating women who have received Mycorzo to measure concentrations of aficamten in breast milk using a validated assay. Assess the effects on the breastfed infant, if available, based on study population.
